narrative.overview: The approved product should feel like a carefully art-directed music object: a cream-and-ink editorial composition where an oversized black record anchors the left, a thin coral orbit tracks real playback, and the song title, real artwork and integrated queue form one calm right-hand composition. The landing page carries the same identity through a large painterly wave. The music is the event; the interface is the frame. The current implementation has already moved away from the earlier dark maroon player: globals.css defines a warm ivory light theme with near-black ink and a warm coral/amber accent. However, the player composition is still the earlier centered stage: a spinning vinyl with a cursor-tilted square album card on top, a Fraunces display title, a bordered 384px queue rail and a coral play button. Those are transitional artifacts, not the approved v1.0 composition.
keyCharacteristics: Current: warm ivory ground, near-black ink, warm coral/amber accent, Fraunces title, centered vinyl + tilted album card, bordered right queue rail.
Approved: warm cream/ivory and near-black ink, coral as the functional accent, blue-violet for secondary metadata, painterly colour only as atmosphere.
Approved: asymmetric editorial player with an oversized cropped black vinyl, separate coral orbit, Inter Light uppercase title, separate square artwork, integrated queue, minimal chrome.
Approved: real room data only; no sample songs, artists, participants or artwork.
Approved: calm, slow motion; accessibility and truthful states are part of the aesthetic.

rules.name: The Ink-and-Cream Rule
rules.body: The approved interface is carried by cream and near-black. Coral and blue-violet are accents, not fields. If a screen reads as coral, violet or gradient-first, it has drifted.

rules.name: The Coral Is Functional Rule
rules.body: In the approved player, coral marks playback progress, the artist line and a small number of active states. It is not a background wash and is not used behind important text.

rules.name: The Current-Is-Not-Approved Rule
rules.body: The current light theme is an intermediate migration. Do not infer the approved composition, typography or component shapes from it.

rules.name: The No-Fraunces Rule
rules.body: Do not use Fraunces for the approved player or redesigned product UI. The approved title is Inter Light, uppercase.

rules.name: The Two-Family Rule
rules.body: Inter and IBM Plex Mono are the approved system. Do not add a third family.

rules.name: The Title Is the Second Focal Point Rule
rules.body: The vinyl is first; the song title is second. Do not let the artist, artwork or queue compete with the title.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: In the approved system, surfaces are flat at rest. Depth comes from tone, spacing and the record's physical mass. Shadows appear only as restrained state feedback, never as decoration.

rules.name: The No-Glass Rule
rules.body: No glassmorphism, frosted panels or glowing UI containers.

rules.name: The Pill-or-Square Rule
rules.body: In the approved system, actions and inputs are pills; artwork and thumbnails are squares. Do not round artwork into cards, and do not square off primary actions.

rules.name: The No-Card-Queue Rule
rules.body: The approved queue is an editorial track listing, not a card, panel or spreadsheet. Do not put each row in its own container.

dos: Do treat sync research/Amply_UI_UX_Design_Notes.md v1.0 as the authoritative visual direction for all UI work.
Do keep the approved interface cream and near-black first, with coral as the functional accent and blue-violet for secondary metadata.
Do keep the approved vinyl black and dominant, with a separate cream/olive centre label.
Do keep vinyl rotation tied to playback state and the orbit marker tied to real playback progress; never derive one from the other.
Do use Inter for the approved UI, Inter Light for the uppercase now-playing title, and IBM Plex Mono for technical metadata.
Do use real room data for titles, thumbnails, participants and durations.
Do preserve the existing backend, sync behaviour and working functionality while the UI/UX phase is in progress.
donts: Don't treat the current centered stage, tilted album card, Fraunces title, coral play button or bordered queue rail as the approved visual direction.
Don't reintroduce the earlier dark maroon/near-black player or a dark right-hand queue sidebar.
Don't use a cursor-following 3D album card or place the album artwork in the centre of the vinyl.
Don't use Fraunces for the approved player or redesigned product UI.
Don't use equal columns, dashboard cards, glass panels or a carded queue.
Don't place a strong multicolour gradient behind important text.
Don't extract album-art colours to control the whole interface.
Don't fabricate songs, artists, participants, artwork or success states.
Don't initiate backend refactoring, playback-timing changes or new feature development during this UI/UX documentation phase.
